The estimate is uncertain and could be materially lower if yields rise sharply or equities fall, and it is not a guarantee.

The range of outcomes is wide, since a recession or a sharp rise in real yields could produce a negative return, and a strong equity rally could produce a much higher one.

The estimate carries wide uncertainty, since equity valuations are near their 52-week highs in the snapshot and returns could be materially lower or higher over two years.

The estimate is wide because the semiconductor and crypto sleeves can fall by half before recovering, and the cash sleeve earns nothing. I hold this as a plausible but uncertain central case rather than a forecast.

Current yields are not supplied, so this is a cautious estimate rather than a claim of certainty; a recession or inflation shock could make the return negative.

An 8% total return is plausible if U.S. growth stays positive but uneven, earnings breadth supports value-oriented businesses, and Alphabet and Adobe stabilize or monetize AI rather than suffer rapid cannibalization. The 31% in short Treasuries, gold, and cash limits upside in a strong equity rally, while a recession could make the result negative.

A 14% total return is plausible if AI compute spending is productively deployed, paid software and search workflows retain customers, consumer demand does not sharply contract, and some of the recent price de-rating reverses without requiring a return to prior highs. Failure of those assumptions could instead produce a large loss.

The 35% cash allocation contributes exactly 0% under the experiment, so this is a modest nominal forecast, not a certainty; an inflation or recession shock could produce a flat or negative result.

A plausible 10% cumulative total return requires the U.S. to avoid a severe recession and a sharp inflation or rate shock, while the selected businesses sustain enough customer demand and cash generation to deliver modest recovery. In that world, diversified equities can compound without a broad multiple boom and the Treasury allocation can accrue interest; the 5% cash position earns nothing. AI disruption, consumer weakness or correlated equity and bond losses could produce a much worse result.

This requires neither every company nor every AI layer to win, but the forecast has wide uncertainty and could instead be sharply negative if spending retrenches, monetization disappoints, or geopolitical and valuation risks dominate.

The estimate is deliberately conservative because several holdings have already delivered large one-year gains and my information is price-only, so a realistic band spans roughly -15% to +20%.

For +18% to be plausible over nine months, three things must hold in the world: the AI and semicap de-rating visible in the snapshot must be positioning and multiple compression rather than a capital-expenditure bust, crude-linked prices must hold most of their 2026 gains so energy cash flows and buybacks continue, and gold and bitcoin must not close durably below their 52-week lows. If the first two hold, the 62% tech sleeve can re-rate 20-30% off its 20-50% discounts while the energy sleeve adds cash yield, which is what this number represents; it is a modal outcome with wide uncertainty, not a bound, and a mirror-image outcome near -25% is entirely possible if hyperscaler capex guidance is cut or crude collapses.

For a roughly 87% defensive-equity and gold book with 13% cash that earns zero, a plausible outcome is a modest positive return in the mid single digits, which requires that nominal growth merely slows rather than contracts, that no systemic credit or geopolitical event forces a broad de-rating of equities, and that staples, healthcare and utilities continue to deliver earnings roughly in line with their historical low-single-digit to mid-single-digit growth. This is a single central estimate, not a guarantee: the same book could reasonably return anywhere from roughly negative 6% in a mild recession or sector derating to roughly positive 12% in a benign disinflationary expansion, and the 13% cash drag caps upside in any strong equity year. I cannot verify valuations, rates or policy at the cutoff, so the estimate leans on the price paths in the packet and on general knowledge rather than on a computed valuation model.

Short-duration carry and modest defensive equity returns should produce a small positive one-month result if rates stay high without a shock, growth slows without recession, and no sharp risk-off event occurs. The estimate is a blend of modest equity, bond and zero cash returns, and the realised outcome could be meaningfully negative or positive.

A one-month return near +2.5% is plausible if semiconductor equipment and AI-infrastructure names stabilize, crypto holds above its 52-week lows, and the washed-out healthcare and industrial names recover some ground. A roughly 2% three-month return is plausible if short and intermediate yields stay range-bound so bond carry accrues, the defensive equity sleeve keeps paying dividends without a large drawdown, and gold holds its level. It would fail if a sharp rate or equity sell-off hit the bonds and defensive sectors together, or if a broad rally left this defensive book lagging. The uncertainty is wide relative to the point estimate, and the figure is not a guarantee.

For the outcome to be plausible, sticky inflation must keep real yields restrictive, the economy must keep slowing without recession, and crowded speculative leaders must not rebound sharply enough to leave the book behind. The estimate is uncertain and could be negative if the market falls, and I have no reliable basis for a precise return figure.

A modest positive three-month return is plausible if semiconductor and refining sentiment stabilizes, small caps find support, and crypto holds its trailing range without a new leg down. The forecast is highly uncertain because the book is concentrated in high-beta assets, and a macro shock could push the outcome well below zero.

This forecast assumes policy rates stay restrictive enough for the bond sleeve to earn its income, growth slows without a deep recession so defensive earnings hold, and gold does not fall sharply. A plausible outcome is a low single-digit gain, but equity or rate shocks could produce a loss, so the estimate carries wide uncertainty.

A plausible nine-month outcome requires that real yields do not rise further, AI infrastructure orders stabilise rather than fall, energy producers keep their discipline, and the crypto cycle recovers partially from its post-peak drawdown. The estimate is highly uncertain, because the book has large correlated exposures to crypto and semiconductor equipment that could fall 30 to 50 percent in a severe risk-off episode, so the realised outcome could be strongly negative as well as strongly positive.

For a 5% twelve-month return, short and intermediate Treasury and aggregate bond income must continue roughly as current yields imply, defensive equities must keep earnings through a slowdown rather than a deep recession, gold must hold or rise modestly, and the broad-market sleeve must not suffer a large drawdown. The estimate is uncertain and could be materially lower if yields rise sharply or equities fall, and it is not a guarantee.

A 6% return assumes that US equities earn a normal return of around 7 to 8% over the year, that short and intermediate bonds earn carry of around 4%, and that gold and energy are roughly flat. This requires US growth to stay positive, real yields to remain stable and no recession, and the cash weight earns nothing. The range of outcomes is wide, since a recession or a sharp rise in real yields could produce a negative return, and a strong equity rally could produce a much higher one.

A positive 12-month outcome requires that AI hardware demand digests without collapsing, that software multiples stabilise as renewal rates hold, that crypto recovers as real rates ease, and that healthcare and energy cash flows hold up. The estimate is highly uncertain, the dispersion across holdings is very wide, and a combined risk-off shock could produce a sharply negative outcome instead.

This requires US and developed earnings to keep growing near nominal GDP, real rates to ease gradually rather than abruptly, and no severe recession before 2028; a moderate growth scare inside the period would lower interim value but is not inconsistent with this outcome. The estimate carries wide uncertainty, since equity valuations are near their 52-week highs in the snapshot and returns could be materially lower or higher over two years.

A 20% cumulative gain over 24 months requires that the AI capex digestion ends by 2027, that memory and equipment earnings recover, that managed-care and medtech margins normalize, and that real rates do not rise further. The estimate is wide because the semiconductor and crypto sleeves can fall by half before recovering, and the cash sleeve earns nothing. I hold this as a plausible but uncertain central case rather than a forecast.

A roughly +0.02% total return is plausible if short-end yields stay broadly stable so SHY's modest income offsets price noise: cash contributes exactly 0% by rule and SHY represents just 15%. Its trailing adjusted total returns of +0.25% over three months and +1.82% over twelve months support only a small starting expectation; a sharp yield rise could make realized performance negative, and the packet does not provide the current yield.

A modest positive return is plausible if broad activity avoids a sudden downturn and value and defensive exposures retain some of their recent relative resilience; the 40% in SHY.US and cash limits upside, and a macroeconomic or rate shock could still make the realized result negative.

The +3% total-return forecast assumes broad equities remain orderly, digital and AI investment is deferred rather than broadly cancelled, and some recent technology underperformance reverses. This is a conditional one-month mean-reversion forecast with substantial downside uncertainty, not a guaranteed outcome.

A total return of about 0.20% is plausible if short-term Treasury yields do not rise materially: SHY.US reported a 0.25% return over the prior three months, and an 80% weight gives a rough portfolio anchor near 0.20% before any new rate move, while cash earns zero. Past returns are a weak guide, and a short-rate shock could make the portfolio return negative.

A +2% total return is plausible if the broad-market pullback remains a correction rather than the start of a recession, value and defensive relative resilience continues, and bond yields do not jump sharply. That scenario is consistent with the positive trailing-12-month returns of the equity exposures in the packet, but near-high prices and three-month uncertainty make this a low-conviction estimate; a joint equity and rate shock could produce a negative outcome.

An 8% total return is plausible if AI, cloud and fabrication spending remain intact, power projects are not broadly deferred, and the United States avoids a credit shock, allowing some of the selected selloffs to reverse; the cash position limits upside, and any of those assumptions could fail.

This modest positive total-return forecast is plausible if U.S. growth slows without a severe recession, bond income accrues without an adverse rate repricing, and defensive equity earnings hold up. The 40% cash allocation earns zero and dilutes gains; because current yields and future earnings are not supplied, the forecast is conditional and the realized return could be negative.

The 6% central forecast is plausible if U.S. activity avoids a deep recession and broad cash flows remain resilient, allowing the 78% equity sleeve to participate while gold, short Treasuries and cash temper risk. It is not an extrapolation of trailing returns: a recession, market-wide repricing or adverse supply shock could instead produce a flat or negative outcome.

The +14% central estimate assumes a partial reversal of price stress if AI and cloud spending continues and investors regain confidence in the monetization of platforms and enterprise software; a rebound across the high-beta holdings could overcome the 15% zero-return cash allocation. It does not assume a full retracement to prior highs, and an AI-capex slowdown, recession, higher real rates, or Taiwan shock could instead produce a substantial loss.

A +3.5% nominal total return is plausible if inflation remains contained, bond rates and credit conditions avoid a sharp adverse repricing, and U.S. earnings stay positive. Bond distributions and modest equity participation could lift the mix, while 15% cash contributes 0% and limits the upside. Current yields are not supplied, so this is a cautious estimate rather than a claim of certainty; a recession or inflation shock could make the return negative.

An 8% total return is plausible if U.S. growth stays positive but uneven, earnings breadth supports value-oriented businesses, and Alphabet and Adobe stabilize or monetize AI rather than suffer rapid cannibalization. The 31% in short Treasuries, gold, and cash limits upside in a strong equity rally, while a recession could make the result negative.

A 14% total return is plausible if AI compute spending is productively deployed, paid software and search workflows retain customers, consumer demand does not sharply contract, and some of the recent price de-rating reverses without requiring a return to prior highs. Failure of those assumptions could instead produce a large loss.

A 6% total return is plausible if the economy avoids a deep recession, rate and credit losses remain contained, bond distributions accrue, and the 20% equity sleeve earns modest positive returns. The 35% cash allocation contributes exactly 0% under the experiment, so this is a modest nominal forecast, not a certainty; an inflation or recession shock could produce a flat or negative result.

A plausible 10% cumulative total return requires the U.S. to avoid a severe recession and a sharp inflation or rate shock, while the selected businesses sustain enough customer demand and cash generation to deliver modest recovery. In that world, diversified equities can compound without a broad multiple boom and the Treasury allocation can accrue interest; the 5% cash position earns nothing. AI disruption, consumer weakness or correlated equity and bond losses could produce a much worse result.

A 22% total return is plausible if AI usage and related compute spending continue, selected holdings recover part of their packet-period price declines, and power investment supports equipment demand. This requires neither every company nor every AI layer to win, but the forecast has wide uncertainty and could instead be sharply negative if spending retrenches, monetization disappoints, or geopolitical and valuation risks dominate.

A one-month expected return of about +0.5 percent is plausible if the observed pattern of defensive leadership and high-beta stress persists: bond and defensive equity sleeves roughly offset any index weakness, gold and cash dampen swings, and the cost of the 8 percent cash drag is small; this forecast would be wrong if either a sharp risk-on rally leaves defensives behind or a broad shock hits bonds, gold and equities together, and the true distribution of one-month outcomes is wide even for a low-risk book.

A roughly +1.5% total return is plausible if, as the snapshot implies, healthcare, staples and dividend value continue to hold relative leadership, short-duration Treasuries keep paying modest carry, and the 26% cash sleeve earns nothing but avoids the single-name drawdowns visible in names falling 20% to 50% over three months; this outcome requires no recession, no sharp rise in long yields and no abrupt re-leadership of AI-capex names, and it is only a central estimate in a market where three-month outcomes for individual instruments range widely, so the realized figure could plausibly land anywhere between roughly -4% and +7%.

The forecast of roughly +4.5% rests on the world in which there is no hard recession, defensive earnings from staples, health care, utilities and franchised cash flows hold up, short-duration Treasuries and the 12% cash buffer carry positive yield-like returns while long duration stays challenged, gold and energy provide modest insurance gains if fiscal or geopolitical risks persist, and the AI-complex de-rating does not turn into a broad market crash; this is a single estimate with wide uncertainty, and if growth-stock leadership resumes the portfolio would likely trail SPY even if its absolute return stays modestly positive.

A modest +5% expected total return is plausible if the world view is roughly right: value, energy and financial cash flows hold up while the AI trade digests, staples and gold cushion drawdowns, and the 15% cash sleeve at 0% dilutes both upside and downside; for this to happen we need no deep recession (so bank credit and energy demand stay intact), real rates that stay high but not spiking, and a rotation that continues at a slower pace than the last twelve months. The estimate is deliberately conservative because several holdings have already delivered large one-year gains and my information is price-only, so a realistic band spans roughly -15% to +20%.

For +18% to be plausible over nine months, three things must hold in the world: the AI and semicap de-rating visible in the snapshot must be positioning and multiple compression rather than a capital-expenditure bust, crude-linked prices must hold most of their 2026 gains so energy cash flows and buybacks continue, and gold and bitcoin must not close durably below their 52-week lows. If the first two hold, the 62% tech sleeve can re-rate 20-30% off its 20-50% discounts while the energy sleeve adds cash yield, which is what this number represents; it is a modal outcome with wide uncertainty, not a bound, and a mirror-image outcome near -25% is entirely possible if hyperscaler capex guidance is cut or crude collapses.

For a roughly 87% defensive-equity and gold book with 13% cash that earns zero, a plausible outcome is a modest positive return in the mid single digits, which requires that nominal growth merely slows rather than contracts, that no systemic credit or geopolitical event forces a broad de-rating of equities, and that staples, healthcare and utilities continue to deliver earnings roughly in line with their historical low-single-digit to mid-single-digit growth. This is a single central estimate, not a guarantee: the same book could reasonably return anywhere from roughly negative 6% in a mild recession or sector derating to roughly positive 12% in a benign disinflationary expansion, and the 13% cash drag caps upside in any strong equity year. I cannot verify valuations, rates or policy at the cutoff, so the estimate leans on the price paths in the packet and on general knowledge rather than on a computed valuation model.

For this roughly 9 percent expected total return to be plausible, the world needs to show that energy stays expensive enough to keep producers and services cash-generative, that the semiconductor order air-pocket is digestion rather than the start of a multi-year bust, and that staples, pharma and telecom keep their earnings resilience; if instead crude collapses toward its 52-week lows and AI capex contracts further, the cyclical sleeves would likely drive the book down double digits, so this is a calibrated middle outcome with wide uncertainty, not a claim of certainty.
